question: Which is the most powerful river in the world in terms of its volume and extensive drainage into the Atlantic Ocean?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amazon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Amazon River is the most powerful river in the world by volume, carrying more water than the next several largest rivers combined. (अमेज़न नदी — सबसे शक्तिशाली नदी)

 

• It discharges an average of about 209,000 cubic metres of water per second into the Atlantic Ocean, accounting for roughly one-fifth of the world's total river flow into the oceans.

 

• The Amazon originates in the Andes Mountains of Peru and flows eastward through Brazil, draining the vast Amazon Basin, the largest drainage basin in the world.

 

• Its extensive drainage network and the sheer volume of freshwater it releases create a noticeable freshwater plume far out into the Atlantic Ocean.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Nile (Africa) is the longest river in the world by length, flowing into the Mediterranean Sea, but it is far smaller than the Amazon in terms of volume.

 

• The Congo River is the second most voluminous river in the world and also drains into the Atlantic Ocean, but its discharge is much less than the Amazon's.

 

NOTE

 

• Congo (Option 1): Second largest river by discharge volume, flowing through Central Africa into the Atlantic, but ranks below the Amazon.

 

• Amur (Option 3): A major river in East Asia forming part of the China-Russia border; it drains into the Sea of Okhotsk (Pacific), not the Atlantic.

 

• Nile (Option 4): The longest river in the world, flowing into the Mediterranean Sea, but with much lower discharge volume than the Amazon.

question:
Which of the following statements about Akshdeep Singh is NOT true?

1. Akshdeep Singh won the National Race Walking Championship.

2. Akshdeep Singh qualified for the Paris 2024 Olympics and World Athletics Championships 2023.

3. Akshdeep Singh won a medal at Nomi in 2023.

4. In the men's 20 km race walk event, Akshdeep Singh clocked 1 hour 19 minutes 55 seconds, a new national record, to win the Silver medal.
option_1: Akshdeep Singh won the National Race Walking Championship.
option_2: Akshdeep Singh qualified for the Paris 2024 Olympics and World Athletics Championships 2023.
option_3: Akshdeep Singh won a medal at Nomi in 2023.
option_4: In the men's 20 km race walk event, Akshdeep Singh clocked 1 hour 19 minutes 55 seconds, a new national record, to win the Silver medal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is In the men's 20 km race walk event, Akshdeep Singh clocked 1 hour 19 minutes 55 seconds, a new national record, to win the Silver medal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Akshdeep Singh is an Indian race walker. At the National Race Walking Championship in Ranchi (February 2023), he clocked 1 hour 19 minutes 55 seconds — a new national record — and this run won him the Gold medal, not the Silver medal. (अक्षदीप सिंह — भारतीय पैदल चाल एथलीट)

 

• Statement 4 is therefore NOT true, because it wrongly attributes a Silver medal to a performance that actually earned him the Gold medal.

 

• Statement 1 is true: Akshdeep Singh has won the National Race Walking Championship (he retained his title with another national record in Chandigarh in January 2024).

 

• Statement 2 is true: He qualified for the Paris 2024 Olympics (mixed marathon race walk relay) and the World Athletics Championships 2023.

 

• Statement 3 is true: He won the gold medal at the 2023 Asian 20km Race Walking Championships held at Nomi, Japan (March 2023), with a time of 1:20:57.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Akshdeep Singh hails from Punjab and trains under coach Gurmeet Singh, himself a former national record holder in race walking.

 

• The 20 km race walk is an Olympic athletics event testing speed, technique, and endurance under strict rules requiring constant ground contact.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: True — he is a National Race Walking Championship title holder.

 

• Option 2: True — he qualified for both the Paris 2024 Olympics and the 2023 World Athletics Championships.

 

• Option 3: True — he won gold at Nomi, Japan in 2023.

question: The law of octaves asserts that every eighth element has comparable properties when grouped in increasing order of their atomic masses and is also known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Newland's relation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Law of Octaves was proposed by the English chemist John Alexander Reina Newlands in 1865 and is also called Newlands' Law of Octaves. (न्यूलैंड्स का अष्टक नियम — रासायनिक तत्वों का वर्गीकरण)

 

• Newlands arranged the known elements in order of increasing atomic mass and observed that every eighth element had properties similar to the first, just like the eighth note in a musical octave repeats the properties of the first note.

 

• This was one of the earliest attempts at classifying elements before the Periodic Table, and it worked reasonably well only for lighter elements (up to calcium).

 

• The law failed for heavier elements because it assumed only 56 elements existed in nature and did not leave room for undiscovered elements.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Newlands' Law of Octaves was later superseded by Dmitri Mendeleev's Periodic Law (1869), which arranged elements by atomic mass but left gaps for undiscovered elements.

 

• Mendeleev is regarded as the father of the modern periodic table's precursor, while Henry Moseley later refined it based on atomic number.

 

NOTE

 

• Gravity relation (Option 1): Not a recognised chemistry classification law; relates to gravitational force, unrelated to periodicity of elements.

 

• Doppler relation (Option 2): Refers to the Doppler Effect in physics, concerning change in wave frequency due to relative motion, unrelated to chemistry classification.

 

• Coulomb's relation (Option 3): Refers to Coulomb's Law of electrostatic force between charges, unrelated to periodic classification of elements.

question: Which of the following regions in India is nicknamed as the storehouse of minerals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chota Nagpur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chota Nagpur Plateau, spread across Jharkhand, parts of Odisha, Chhattisgarh and West Bengal, is called the "storehouse of minerals" of India. (छोटानागपुर पठार — खनिजों का भंडार)

 

• It holds vast reserves of coal, iron ore, mica, bauxite, copper, and manganese, making it India's most important mineral belt.

 

• Major mining and industrial centres such as Jamshedpur, Bokaro, and Dhanbad are located within this region, which also hosts key coalfields like Jharia and Raniganj.

 

• The plateau's rich mineral wealth has made it the backbone of India's iron and steel and coal-based industries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Deccan Plateau is known for black cotton soil (regur soil) and basaltic Deccan Trap formations, ideal for cotton cultivation.

 

• The Western Ghats are recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage biodiversity hotspot, not primarily for mineral wealth.

 

NOTE

 

• Deccan Plateau (Option 1): Known for black soil and volcanic basalt rock, not primarily minerals.

 

• Western Ghats (Option 2): Known for biodiversity and rainfall-bearing hill ranges along India's west coast.

 

• Himalayas (Option 4): Known for being the world's youngest fold mountains and a source of major rivers, not a mineral storehouse.

question: Which of the following is consistent with import substitution policy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tariffs and quotas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Import substitution is an economic policy that seeks to replace foreign imports with domestic production by protecting local industries from foreign competition. (आयात प्रतिस्थापन नीति — शुल्क और कोटा)

 

• The primary tools used to implement import substitution are tariffs (import duties) and quotas (quantitative restrictions), which make imported goods costlier or limit their quantity, thereby encouraging consumers to buy domestically produced goods.

 

• India followed an import substitution industrialisation (ISI) strategy, particularly from the 1950s to the 1980s, to build up domestic industry behind protective trade barriers.

 

• This is the opposite of an export-promotion or open, liberalised trade policy that emphasises free flow of goods and capital.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India shifted away from import substitution towards trade liberalisation after the 1991 economic reforms.

 

• Convertibility (capital or current account) refers to the freedom to convert domestic currency into foreign currency for transactions, which is a liberalisation measure, not a protectionist one.

 

NOTE

 

• Capital account convertibility (Option 1): Relates to free movement of capital across borders, a liberalisation measure, not protectionist.

 

• Flexible exchange rate policy (Option 2): Lets the market determine currency value; not a tool of import substitution.

 

• Current account convertibility (Option 4): Allows free conversion of currency for trade in goods and services, again a liberalisation measure, not protectionist.

question:
Which of the following will be considered as normal residents of India?

A) Indians working in foreign embassies in India

B) Ambassador for India in rest of the world
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A normal resident of a country is a person or institution that normally resides in that country and whose centre of economic interest lies there. (सामान्य निवासी — केंद्र आर्थिक हित)

 

• The standard exclusion from normal residency applies to foreign nationals posted as diplomatic/embassy staff of another country — they remain normal residents of the country their embassy represents, not of the host country.

 

• Statement A refers to Indian citizens employed in a foreign embassy located in India — since they are Indian nationals whose centre of economic interest (home, family, spending) remains in India, they continue to be treated as normal residents of India.

 

• Statement B refers to India's own ambassador posted abroad — such a person continues to represent India's interests and remains a normal resident of India despite physically residing outside the country, similar to armed forces personnel or diplomats posted overseas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• In contrast, foreign diplomats and embassy staff of other countries stationed in India are treated as normal residents of their own home country, not of India, for national income accounting purposes.

 

• Similarly, staff of international organisations (UN, IMF, World Bank) located in a country are not treated as normal residents of that host country.

 

NOTE

 

• Only A (Option 1): Incomplete — it wrongly excludes Statement B, which is also a valid case of a normal resident of India.

 

• Only B (Option 2): Incomplete — it wrongly excludes Statement A, which also qualifies as a normal resident of India.

 

• Neither A nor B (Option 4): Incorrect — both statements describe genuine cases of normal residents of India.

question: Which of the following is the most problematic and primary difficulty of barter exchanges as against money-based exchanges?
option_1: Bartered exchanges involve difficulty in preserving value.
option_2: Barter exchanges may result in an incorrect valuation of the goods transacted.
option_3: Barter exchanges may be imperfectly divisible.
option_4: Barter exchanges require a double coincidence of wants.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Barter exchanges require a double coincidence of wants.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The most fundamental and primary drawback of the barter system is the requirement of a "double coincidence of wants" — both parties must simultaneously want what the other has to offer. (वस्तु विनिमय — इच्छाओं का दोहरा संयोग)

 

• Without this double coincidence, a direct exchange of goods for goods cannot take place at all, making barter highly inefficient as an economy grows more complex.

 

• The introduction of money solved this problem by acting as a common medium of exchange, so a seller need not find someone who wants exactly what they are selling and simultaneously has what they want in return.

 

• Other issues like difficulty in storing value, indivisibility of goods, and difficulty in valuation are also drawbacks of barter, but they are secondary problems that stem from or compound the primary issue of the double coincidence of wants.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Money performs four key functions: medium of exchange, store of value, unit of account, and standard of deferred payment — all of which barter struggles to fulfil.

 

• Historically, barter economies were limited to small, simple, self-sufficient communities precisely because of this coordination problem.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (difficulty in preserving value): A genuine limitation of barter (perishable goods can't store value), but not the primary/most fundamental one.

 

• Option 2 (incorrect valuation): A real problem due to lack of a common unit of account, but secondary to the double coincidence issue.

 

• Option 3 (imperfectly divisible): Indivisibility of goods (e.g., a cow cannot be split for a small transaction) is a genuine limitation, but not the most primary difficulty.

question: Who among the following personalities is a professional Kuchipudi Dancer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kaushalya Reddy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kaushalya Reddy is a renowned Indian Kuchipudi dancer, celebrated as a leading exponent of the classical dance form along with her husband, Raja Reddy. (कौशल्या रेड्डी — कुचिपुड़ी नृत्यांगना)

 

• Kuchipudi is a classical dance form that originated in the village of Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh, characterised by fast rhythmic footwork and expressive gestures (abhinaya).

 

• Kaushalya Reddy and Raja Reddy together have been instrumental in popularising Kuchipudi across India and internationally, and have received honours including the Padma Shri.

 

• They also founded the Natyatarangini dance institution in Delhi to train new generations of Kuchipudi dancers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other renowned Kuchipudi exponents include Yamini Krishnamurthy and Vempati Chinna Satyam, who is regarded as a father figure of modern Kuchipudi.

 

• India's major classical dance forms include Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Sattriya, and Kuchipudi.

 

NOTE

 

• Radha Sridhar (Option 1): An Indian classical dancer/choreographer known for her work with Chandralekha in contemporary and Bharatanatyam-based dance, not primarily Kuchipudi.

 

• Surupa Sen (Option 2): A celebrated Odissi dancer and principal dancer/choreographer at Nrityagram.

 

• Anupama Hoskere (Option 3): Known for her work in puppetry and theatre, not Kuchipudi dance.

question: Which region has the maximum concentration of Iron and Steel industries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chota Nagpur Plateau.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chota Nagpur Plateau region has the maximum concentration of iron and steel industries in India. (छोटानागपुर पठार — लौह-इस्पात उद्योग)

 

• This is due to the ready and abundant local availability of key raw materials — iron ore, coal, manganese, and limestone — all found in close proximity within the region.

 

• Major steel plants located here include Tata Steel (Jamshedpur), Bokaro Steel Plant, and IISCO (Burnpur), forming what is often called India's "steel belt" or the Chota Nagpur-Damodar Valley industrial region.

 

• The region spans parts of Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Odisha, with excellent rail connectivity aiding raw material transport.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's first modern integrated steel plant, Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO), was established at Jamshedpur in 1907 in this very region.

 

• Other public sector steel plants set up here include Bokaro (Jharkhand) and Durgapur/Burnpur (West Bengal).

 

NOTE

 

• Shillong Plateau (Option 1): Located in Meghalaya, known for its scenic plateau and coal/limestone reserves, but not a major iron-steel hub.

 

• Deccan Plateau (Option 2): Known for black cotton soil and basaltic rock, not concentrated iron-steel industries.

 

• Malwa Plateau (Option 4): Located in Madhya Pradesh, known for black soil and cotton cultivation, not iron-steel industry concentration.

question: Who among the following has been accused of committing the judicial murder of Raja Nand Kumar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Warren Hastings.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Warren Hastings, the first Governor-General of Bengal, is accused by historians of orchestrating the "judicial murder" of Maharaja Nandakumar (Raja Nand Kumar) in 1775. (वारेन हेस्टिंग्स — नंदकुमार का न्यायिक हत्या)

 

• Nandakumar had accused Hastings of corruption and bribery; soon after, he was tried on an unrelated, decades-old charge of forgery by the Supreme Court under Chief Justice Sir Elijah Impey, a close friend of Hastings.

 

• Nandakumar was found guilty and hanged in August 1775, despite forgery not normally being a capital offence under existing Hindu/Mughal law in Bengal — leading many historians to regard the episode as a case of judicial murder aimed at silencing Hastings' accuser.

 

• The incident significantly damaged Hastings' reputation and later became one of the charges against him during his impeachment trial in England (1788-1795).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Warren Hastings governed British India from 1772 to 1785 and was central to institutionalising British administration, including judicial and revenue reforms.

 

• He was eventually acquitted after his long impeachment trial led by Edmund Burke, though the trial ruined him financially.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Wellesly (Option 1): Known for introducing the Subsidiary Alliance system; not connected to the Nandakumar case.

 

• Lord Dalhousie (Option 2): Known for the Doctrine of Lapse; governed decades after this episode.

 

• Lord Cornwallis (Option 3): Known for the Permanent Settlement of Bengal (1793) and administrative/police reforms; not connected to the Nandakumar case.

question: In which year did Swami Dayanand Saraswati establish Arya Samaj?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1875.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay (Mumbai) in 1875. (आर्य समाज — स्वामी दयानंद सरस्वती, 1875)

 

• The Arya Samaj was a Hindu reform movement based on the infallibility of the Vedas, advocating a return to Vedic principles and opposing idol worship, caste discrimination, child marriage, and untouchability.

 

• Its motto, "Krinvanto Vishwaram Aryam" ("Make this world noble"), reflected its reformist and universalist outlook.

 

• Dayanand Saraswati also authored "Satyarth Prakash" (The Light of Truth), which laid out the core philosophy of the Arya Samaj.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Arya Samaj later established the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) chain of schools and colleges to promote modern education along with Vedic values.

 

• Other contemporary reform movements include the Brahmo Samaj (Raja Ram Mohan Roy, 1828) and the Prarthana Samaj (1867, Bombay).

 

NOTE

 

• 1867 (Option 2): Year of founding of the Prarthana Samaj in Bombay, not the Arya Samaj.

 

• 1828 (Option 3): Year of founding of the Brahmo Sabha (later Brahmo Samaj) by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, not the Arya Samaj.

 

• 1887 (Option 4): Not associated with the founding of any major reform organisation relevant here.

question:
Which of the following is a transfer payment?

a) Unemployment allowances

b) Scholarships

c) Retirement pension
option_2: All of a, b and c
solution_text:
The correct answer is All of a, b and c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A transfer payment is a payment made by the government (or an institution) to an individual without any corresponding productive service being rendered in return during that period. (हस्तांतरण भुगतान — बिना सेवा के भुगतान)

 

• Unemployment allowances (a): Paid to jobless individuals with no current productive service rendered in return — a classic transfer payment.

 

• Scholarships (b): Financial assistance given to students for education, with no current productive service rendered in exchange — a transfer payment.

 

• Retirement pension (c): Paid to retired persons; since no current productive activity is performed by the recipient at the time of payment, it is also classified as a transfer payment (unlike a wage/salary, which compensates for current production).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common examples of transfer payments include old-age pensions, sickness/disability benefits, and subsidies.

 

• Transfer payments are excluded while calculating National Income via the product/income method, since they don't correspond to any current addition to output.

 

NOTE

 

• Only a (Option 1): Too narrow — incorrectly excludes scholarships and retirement pension, which are also transfer payments.

 

• Only a and b (Option 3): Incorrectly excludes retirement pension, which also qualifies as a transfer payment.

 

• Only c (Option 4): Incorrectly excludes unemployment allowances and scholarships, both of which are also transfer payments.

question: Which equation was verified by American scientists Nichols and Hull in 1903 by measuring the radiation pressure of visible light?
solution_text:
The correct answer is P = U/C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• American physicists Ernest Fox Nichols and Gordon Ferrie Hull experimentally verified the theoretical prediction of radiation pressure in the early 1900s, confirming Maxwell's electromagnetic theory. (विकिरण दाब — निकोल्स और हल का प्रयोग)

 

• The formula they confirmed is P = U/C, where P is the radiation pressure, U is the energy flux/intensity of the radiation falling on a surface, and C is the speed of light.

 

• Using a delicately suspended torsion balance (a radiometer-like setup), they measured the minute pressure exerted by light striking a surface, matching Maxwell's theoretical predictions.

 

• This experiment provided strong evidence supporting the electromagnetic wave theory of light and the concept that light carries momentum.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Radiation pressure on a perfectly reflecting surface is double that on a perfectly absorbing surface, i.e., P = 2U/C for reflection.

 

• The concept of light exerting pressure is also the working principle behind proposed solar sail spacecraft propulsion technology.

 

NOTE

 

• Pr = C/N (Option 1): Not a recognised physical formula relevant to radiation pressure.

 

• P = L/M (Option 2): Does not correspond to the radiation pressure relation; not dimensionally or physically relevant here.

 

• P = F/A (Option 3): This is simply the general definition of mechanical pressure (force per unit area), not the specific radiation pressure relation verified by Nichols and Hull.

question:
Match the items in list I with those in list II.

Measure of Money Supply — Formula

i. M1 — a. M1 + Td

ii. M2 — b. Cp + Dd + Od

iii. M3 — c. M3 + TPOd

iv. M4 — d. M1 + POSBd
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-b, ii-d, iii-a, iv-c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) defines four measures of money supply based on increasing liquidity: M1, M2, M3, and M4. (मुद्रा आपूर्ति के मापक — RBI)

 

• M1 = Cp + Dd + Od (Currency with the public + Demand deposits with banks + Other deposits with RBI) — matches i-b.

 

• M2 = M1 + Post Office Savings Bank deposits (POSBd) — matches ii-d.

 

• M3 = M1 + Time deposits with banks (Td) — matches iii-a. M3 is also known as Aggregate Monetary Resources (AMR) and is the most widely used measure.

 

• M4 = M3 + Total deposits with Post Office savings organisations, excluding NSCs (TPOd) — matches iv-c, making M4 the broadest and least liquid measure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Liquidity decreases as we move from M1 to M4 (M1 is the most liquid, M4 the least liquid).

 

• M3 (Broad Money) is the most commonly used indicator for monitoring money supply growth and inflation trends in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (i-d, ii-a, iii-c, iv-b): Incorrectly swaps the formulas; does not match RBI's actual definitions.

 

• Option 3 (i-a, ii-d, iii-b, iv-c): Wrongly assigns M1 the Td-based formula, which actually belongs to M3.

 

• Option 4 (i-c, ii-b, iii-a, iv-d): Wrongly assigns M1 the TPOd-based formula, which actually belongs to M4.

question: Sheorinarayan fair is held in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sheorinarayan (Shivrinarayan) Fair is held in the town of Shivrinarayan in the Janjgir-Champa district of Chhattisgarh. (शिवरीनारायण मेला — छत्तीसगढ़)

 

• It is one of the largest and oldest fairs of Chhattisgarh, organised annually around Magh Purnima, at the confluence of the Mahanadi, Shivnath, and Jonk rivers, referred to locally as "Chhattisgarh's Prayag".

 

• The fair is centred around the Shivrinarayan Temple, dedicated to Lord Vishnu, and draws large numbers of pilgrims and traders.

 

• It is an important cultural and religious event reflecting the traditions of the Chhattisgarh region.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known fairs of Chhattisgarh include the Rajim Kumbh Mela, also held at a river confluence (Triveni Sangam) in Rajim.

 

• Chhattisgarh, formed in 2000 by bifurcation from Madhya Pradesh, is known for its rich tribal culture and numerous river-confluence fairs (melas).

 

NOTE

 

• West Bengal (Option 1): Known for fairs like the Gangasagar Mela, not the Sheorinarayan fair.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 2): Known for tribal fairs like Sarhul, not the Sheorinarayan fair.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 4): From which Chhattisgarh was carved out in 2000; the Sheorinarayan fair belongs to present-day Chhattisgarh, not MP.

question: Where is Bhimrao Ambedkar Multipurpose Stadium situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Faizabad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar (International) Multipurpose/Sports Stadium is situated in Faizabad, in the Ayodhya district of Uttar Pradesh. (डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर स्टेडियम — फैजाबाद)

 

• It is located on the Ayodhya-Sultanpur road, close to the Ayodhya ring road and Ayodhya Airport.

 

• Built to international standards, the stadium includes facilities such as a multipurpose hall and a swimming pool, and forms part of a broader sports infrastructure development in the Ayodhya region.

 

• It is named in honour of Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar, the chief architect of the Indian Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Several sports facilities across India are named after Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, including the Dr. Ambedkar Stadium in New Delhi (football) and stadiums in other cities.

 

• Ayodhya (Faizabad) has seen significant infrastructure development in recent years, including its airport and railway station.

 

NOTE

 

• Ghaziabad (Option 2): Not the location of this stadium; a separate NCR city in Uttar Pradesh.

 

• Kanpur (Option 3): Known for the Green Park Stadium (cricket), not this stadium.

 

• Patna (Option 4): Known for the Moin-ul-Haq Stadium, not this stadium.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution has the idea that 'No child below the age of fourteen years shall be employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 24.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 24 of the Indian Constitution, part of the Fundamental Rights (Right against Exploitation), states that no child below the age of 14 years shall be employed to work in any factory, mine, or other hazardous employment. (अनुच्छेद 24 — बाल श्रम निषेध)

 

• This provision aims to protect children from exploitative and dangerous labour conditions and promote their right to education and healthy development.

 

• It falls under Articles 23-24, which together constitute the Right against Exploitation, prohibiting human trafficking, forced labour (Article 23), and child labour in hazardous work (Article 24).

 

• This constitutional safeguard is further reinforced by laws like the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 (amended 2016).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 21A, inserted by the 86th Amendment (2002), guarantees free and compulsory education to children aged 6 to 14 years, complementing Article 24.

 

• The Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24) is one of the six categories of Fundamental Rights under Part III of the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 22 (Option 1): Provides protection against arbitrary arrest and detention, unrelated to child labour.

 

• Article 19 (Option 3): Guarantees six fundamental freedoms (speech, assembly, movement, etc.), unrelated to child labour.

 

• Article 20 (Option 4): Provides protection in respect of conviction for offences (ex-post-facto law, double jeopardy, self-incrimination), unrelated to child labour.

question: Totaram Sharma is associated with which of the following instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pakhawaj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Tota Ram Sharma is a noted Indian classical musician associated with the Pakhawaj, a barrel-shaped, double-headed percussion instrument. (तोताराम शर्मा — पखावज वादक)

 

• He was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Hindustani Instrumental Music (Pakhawaj) in recognition of his contribution to the art form.

 

• The Pakhawaj is the primary percussion accompaniment for Dhrupad vocal music and for classical dance forms such as Odissi and Kathak (in certain traditions), predating the tabla.

 

• Pakhawaj traditions/gharanas include lineages centred around regions like Nathdwara with roots in Jaipur.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Pakhawaj is played horizontally on the lap or on a stand, with both hands striking the two ends, unlike the tabla, which is a pair of separate drums.

 

• Other noted Pakhawaj players include Pandit Ayodhya Prasad and various exponents from the traditional Pakhawaj gharanas.

 

NOTE

 

• Tanpura (Option 1): A drone string instrument used to provide a continuous harmonic background in Indian classical music, not associated with Totaram Sharma.

 

• Panchavadyam (Option 2): A traditional Kerala percussion ensemble of five instruments, unrelated to Totaram Sharma.

 

• Sarangi (Option 4): A bowed string instrument closely associated with vocal accompaniment; not linked to Totaram Sharma.

question: The founders of Vijayanagara Empire were the feudatories of which of the following dynasties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kakatiya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The founders of the Vijayanagara Empire, Harihara I and Bukka Raya I, were originally officials/feudatories serving under the Kakatiya dynasty of Warangal before the empire's founding in 1336 CE. (कर्ताकीय वंश — विजयनगर साम्राज्य के संस्थापक)

 

• After the fall of the Kakatiya kingdom to the Delhi Sultanate (Muhammad bin Tughlaq), Harihara and Bukka were taken to Delhi, and later sent back to the Deccan to help administer the region for the Sultanate.

 

• With the guidance of the sage Vidyaranya, they re-established Hindu rule in the region and founded the city of Vijayanagara on the banks of the Tungabhadra River in 1336 CE.

 

• The empire went on to become one of the greatest South Indian powers, ruled successively by the Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu dynasties.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first ruler and founder-dynasty of Vijayanagara was the Sangama dynasty, established by Harihara I.

 

• The empire reached its zenith under Krishnadevaraya of the Tuluva dynasty in the early 16th century.

 

NOTE

 

• Hoysala (Option 1): An earlier Karnataka-based dynasty (famous for temples like Belur and Halebidu); not the dynasty the Vijayanagara founders served under.

 

• Pandya (Option 2): A Tamil dynasty of the far south; unrelated to the origins of Harihara and Bukka.

 

• Chola (Option 4): A powerful South Indian dynasty that had already declined by the time of Vijayanagara's founding; unrelated to its founders' origins.

question: The Pakhawaj syllables are primarily used to conclude which of the following Indian classical dances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Odissi dance, compositions are traditionally concluded using rhythmic syllables (bols) of the Pakhawaj, the primary percussion instrument accompanying this classical dance form. (ओडिसी नृत्य — पखावज बोल)

 

• The Pakhawaj provides the fundamental rhythmic (tala) structure for Odissi, and dancers often perform footwork patterns that directly echo the Pakhawaj's bols, especially in the concluding portions of a piece.

 

• Odissi originated in the temples of Odisha, particularly associated with the Jagannath Temple, Puri, and blends devotional (bhakti) themes with intricate body movements (tribhangi).

 

• This close relationship between Pakhawaj syllables and dance movement is a distinctive feature that sets Odissi's percussion tradition apart from tabla-accompanied forms like Kathak.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Renowned Odissi exponents include Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sonal Mansingh, and Sanjukta Panigrahi.

 

• Other classical dance-instrument pairings: Kathak is usually accompanied by the tabla, while Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi typically use the mridangam.

 

NOTE

 

• Manipuri (Option 1): Uses the Pung (Manipuri drum) as its primary percussion accompaniment, not Pakhawaj syllables to conclude the dance.

 

• Kathak (Option 2): Primarily accompanied by the tabla, with compositions often concluding with tabla bols (tihais), not Pakhawaj.

 

• Kathakali (Option 4): A dance-drama from Kerala accompanied mainly by the Chenda and Maddalam, not Pakhawaj.

question: Who among the following was a member of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr. KM Munshi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly was constituted on 29 August 1947, chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, to prepare the draft Constitution of India. (प्रारूप समिति — डॉ. के. एम. मुंशी)

 

• Dr. K.M. Munshi was one of the seven original members of the Drafting Committee, appointed at its formation, and played a key role in the drafting process.

 

• The other original members were N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, Syed Mohammad Saadullah, N. Madhava Rau (who later replaced B.L. Mitter), and T.T. Krishnamachari (who later replaced D.P. Khaitan after his death).

 

• Munshi's legal expertise and drafting skills made significant contributions to shaping key constitutional provisions, particularly the Fundamental Rights.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sir B.N. Rao served as the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly and prepared the original draft, but he was not a formal member of the Drafting Committee itself.

 

• The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India on 26 November 1949, which came into effect on 26 January 1950.

 

NOTE

 

• BN Rao (Option 2): Served as Constitutional Advisor who prepared the initial draft used by the Drafting Committee, but was not himself a member of the Committee.

 

• TT Krishnamachari (Option 3): Though he did later join the Committee as a replacement for D.P. Khaitan, the intended/original and most closely associated founding member here is Munshi.

 

• N Madhav Rau (Option 4): Similarly joined later as a replacement for B.L. Mitter due to the latter's ill health.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

question: In March 2023, the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) amended the 2015 PFRDA Regulation to increase the age limit for the Ombudsman from 65 to ____ years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 70.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In March 2023, the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) amended the PFRDA (Redressal of Subscriber Grievance) Regulations, 2015, to raise the upper age limit for the Ombudsman from 65 years to 70 years. (पीएफआरडीए — लोकपाल आयु सीमा 70 वर्ष)

 

• The amendment aimed to widen the eligible candidate pool for the Ombudsman post by allowing experienced, older professionals to be considered for appointment.

 

• The PFRDA Ombudsman mechanism is responsible for the redressal of grievances of subscribers under the National Pension System (NPS).

 

• This change was notified by the Central Government via a formal amendment to the 2015 regulations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• PFRDA was established in 2003 and given statutory status through the PFRDA Act, 2013, to regulate and develop the pension sector in India, including the National Pension System (NPS).

 

• The current Chairperson and headquarters details of PFRDA (New Delhi) are regularly tested in current affairs-based GK questions.

 

NOTE

 

• 77 (Option 1): Not the age limit specified in this 2023 amendment.

 

• 80 (Option 2): Not the age limit specified in this 2023 amendment.

 

• 90 (Option 4): Not the age limit specified in this 2023 amendment.

question: The literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh state as per the Census of 2011 is _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 67.02%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India, 2011, the overall literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh (undivided, prior to Telangana's bifurcation in 2014) was 67.02%. (आंध्र प्रदेश साक्षरता दर — 67.02%, जनगणना 2011)

 

• The male literacy rate stood at approximately 74.88%, while the female literacy rate was approximately 59.15%, reflecting a notable gender gap.

 

• This figure was lower than the national literacy rate of 74.04% recorded in Census 2011, placing undivided Andhra Pradesh among the states with comparatively lower literacy levels.

 

• The Census 2011 was the 15th Census of India and the last decadal census conducted so far.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate among Indian states in Census 2011, while Bihar recorded the lowest.

 

• The state of Andhra Pradesh was bifurcated in 2014 to create the new state of Telangana.

 

NOTE

 

• 66.48% (Option 1): Not the officially recorded Census 2011 figure for Andhra Pradesh.

 

• 66% (Option 3): An approximated but incorrect figure; the precise Census 2011 figure is 67.02%.

 

• 68.5% (Option 4): Not the officially recorded Census 2011 figure for Andhra Pradesh.

question: In which year did Rudolf Ludwig Karl Virchow formulate his famous aphorism 'Omnis cellula-e cellula' which became a part of the foundation of cell theory?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1855.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• German scientist Rudolf Ludwig Karl Virchow formulated the famous Latin aphorism "Omnis cellula-e cellula" ("every cell originates from another existing cell like it") in 1855. (रुडोल्फ विरचो — कोशिका सिद्धांत, 1855)

 

• This principle became a critical third tenet of Cell Theory, extending the earlier work of Matthias Schleiden and Theodor Schwann (1838-39), who had proposed that all living organisms are composed of cells but had not addressed how new cells arise.

 

• Virchow's contribution established that cells do not arise spontaneously but only through the division of pre-existing cells, refuting the theory of spontaneous generation at the cellular level.

 

• Virchow is also widely regarded as the father of modern pathology for his work linking cellular changes to disease.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The complete modern Cell Theory thus rests on three principles: (1) all living organisms are composed of cells, (2) the cell is the basic unit of life, and (3) all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

 

• Virchow's other major contributions include work in cellular pathology, public health, and anthropology.

 

NOTE

 

• 1869 (Option 2): Not the year associated with Virchow's aphorism.

 

• 1840 (Option 3): Close to but predates the actual formulation; also close to Schleiden-Schwann's cell theory (1838-39), not Virchow's addition.

 

• 1835 (Option 4): Predates the accepted cell theory formulations altogether.
